newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX mulls gold and silver warehouses abroad.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX mulls gold and silver warehouses abroad.

text.p: New York Mercantile Exchange is looking to open warehouses abroad in Europe and the Far East as delivery points for COMEX gold and silver futures contracts, NYMEX President Patrick Thompson said.
"Certainly we would look to have a strong European leg and a strong Asia-Pacific leg to it," Thompson told Reuters.
Likely locations would be Zurich, London and Hong Kong.

Tuesday, NYMEX said the COMEX copper advisory committee had decided to open a warehouse in Chile for delivery of its copper futures contract. No start-up date was announced. COMEX is a division of NYMEX.
In the short term, the exchange's copper contract faced most competition, and a therefore foreign warehouse to store red metal was the priority, Thompson said.
"But the general overall business plan is to also carry this forward for silver and gold at a later date," he said.
COMEX copper faced stiffer competition when rival London Metal Exchange opened warehouses for copper in the United States.
"First and foremost with the metals, it is going through the entire copper analysis and using that as a model for proceeding on from there," Thompson said.
